body.deadline_description: Wage Payment Act governs pay frequency and final pay: K.S.A. 44-313 to 44-327 require regular pay intervals (at least semimonthly) and timely final payment on separation; notice of pay-rate changes required before work is performed (K.S.A. 44-320, K.A.R. 49-20-1).

citation.note: Noncompetes remain common law; non-solicits are now partly statutory: Non-compete agreements are enforced solely under common-law reasonableness (Weber v. Tillman) — K.S.A.

body.rule: Noncompetes remain common law; non-solicits are now partly statutory: Non-compete agreements are enforced solely under common-law reasonableness (Weber v. Tillman) — K.S.A. 50-163 does not reach them. 2025 SB 241 (eff. 2025-07-01) amended K.S.A. 50-163 to presume enforceable two categories of non-solicitation covenant (employee non-solicits protecting confidential/trade-secret information or ≤2 years; customer non-solicits limited to material-contact customers and ≤2 years) and to require reformation of overbroad ones.

body.test_description: Contractor vs. Employee Classification: Kansas recognizes the ABC test for unemployment insurance purposes (K.S.A. § 44-701 et seq.) similar to other states. Control over work methods, provision of tools, integration into the business, and permanence determine status. Misclassification exposes employers to wage-and-hour audits and unemployment insurance liabilities.
